Declare an API token target

Source: R/oauth_token_target.R
oauth_token_target.Rd

Build one entry for oauth_client()'s token_targets. Give the entry a name in that list, such as calendar, then select it with a connection method's target argument. Plain named lists with the same fields are also accepted.

Usage

oauth_token_target(
  resource,
  scopes,
  required_scopes = character(),
  resource_ids = character(),
  scope_aliases = character()
)

Arguments

resource

Exact API identifier sent to the authorization provider: an absolute URI, such as "urn:example:calendar", or a Microsoft application GUID. This identifies the token's audience; HTTP destinations are configured separately through client resource_bases.

scopes

Non-empty character vector of requested API permissions. A space-separated string is also accepted. Identity and refresh-consent scopes belong in client scopes.

required_scopes

Minimum permissions for this API, default character(). The default permits reduced grants; specify the permissions that every usable token for this target must cover.

resource_ids

Names of approved client resource_bases associated with this target. Optional when only exporting tokens to another R package.

scope_aliases

Optional Microsoft short permission names used in token responses. See oauth_client() for provider-specific restrictions.

Value

A plain named list suitable for an entry in token_targets.

Details

This helper checks field syntax and size limits. Client construction checks provider support, scope coverage, API associations and relationships between targets. It preserves the resource identifier exactly and normalizes scopes into distinct tokens.

Examples

oauth_token_target(
  "urn:example:calendar",
  c("calendar.read", "calendar.write"),
  required_scopes = "calendar.read",
  resource_ids = "calendar_api"
)
#> $resource
#> [1] "urn:example:calendar"
#> 
#> $scopes
#> [1] "calendar.read"  "calendar.write"
#> 
#> $required_scopes
#> [1] "calendar.read"
#> 
#> $resource_ids
#> [1] "calendar_api"
#>
